_readme: Golden set for history retrieval. `cards` is a hand-built corpus shaped like the
real one (commits incl. a reverted pair, ah sessions with verified/blocked/failed
endings, harness journals with verbatim stage detail, skills and CLAUDE.md-style
docs, plus cross-project noise). `golden` is (query -> expected card id) with the
editorial reason the expected card is the best answer, written BEFORE measuring.
Labels are judgements about the corpus, not observations of the ranker: if the
ranker misses one, the ranker is wrong, not the label.
`twins` names the pair used for the verified-vs-failed property test.

Fifteen near-identical nightly journals are deliberate: the real corpus is full of templated runs that share one generic title, and a ranker that lets them crowd out the single journal whose stage detail answers the query is the failure mode that dominates it.

cards.title: ah house rules
cards.text:
ah house rules

Every module opens with a comment saying why it exists, not what it does.
No default exports. Errors cross a module boundary as values, never as
throws. Tests live in test/ and are named after the seam they cover, not the
file. Never widen a frozen contract in src/history/types.ts without bumping
INDEX_VERSION.

cards.title: Contributing to ah
cards.text:
Contributing to ah

Commit messages use a conventional prefix: feat, fix, chore, refactor, docs,
perf or test, then a colon and a lowercase summary in the imperative. A
revert keeps the reverted subject verbatim in quotes so the history index can
pair the two. One logical change per commit; a commit that needs the word
"and" is usually two commits.

cards.title: Writing a tool adapter
cards.text:
Writing a tool adapter

An adapter never throws. It returns a typed result whose error arm carries a
message the model can act on, because a thrown adapter kills the turn and the
model learns nothing. Validate arguments with typebox at the boundary, and
keep the network call in its own function so it can be faked in tests.

cards.title: Running the verification gate locally
cards.text:
Running the verification gate locally

ah gate --dry runs the checks without a verdict. A block verdict needs a named
regression: a check that merely warns must never block, or the gate becomes
something people route around.

cards.title: Why the session store is append-only ndjson
cards.text:
Why the session store is append-only ndjson

A transcript is written by a process that can be killed at any moment, so the
format has to survive a torn write. Append-only ndjson does: a half-written
last line is dropped on read and every earlier turn is still there. A
database would give us seeks we do not need and a lock we cannot hold across
concurrent watch writers. If this is ever revisited, the requirement to beat
is crash-safety, not read speed.

cards.title: ADR 0007: BM25 instead of embeddings for history retrieval
cards.text:
ADR 0007: BM25 instead of embeddings for history retrieval

Retrieval has to run on every keystroke of a task description, offline, with
no service to operate and no vectors to store. BM25 over an in-memory
inverted index costs milliseconds on a few thousand cards. Embeddings would
buy synonym recall we can approximate with identifier splitting and trigram
fuzzing, at the price of an index that has to be rebuilt by a model. Revisit
only if recall on prose queries is measured and found wanting.

cards.title: History retrieval: cards, ranking and the walkthrough
cards.text:
History retrieval: cards, ranking and the walkthrough

One card shape covers commits, sessions, journals, docs and skills. The
ranker multiplies lexical score by recency, outcome, path overlap and a
caller-supplied kind boost. The walkthrough runs four differently-weighted
searches, because precedent, attempts, conventions and traps are not the same
question asked four times.

cards.title: Watch mode and the attempt ledger
cards.text:
Watch mode and the attempt ledger

Unattended runs record every attempt as a fact, so a second attempt at the
same task can see what the first one did. The tick is single-flight by
design: overlapping ticks were the original source of ordering bugs.

cards.title: prime-agent house rules
cards.text:
prime-agent house rules

Use pnpm. Every handler validates its payload. Errors are thrown here and
caught at the edge; do not copy ah's value-returning convention into this
repo.

cards.title: ah — an autonomous coding agent with abagraph as its brain
cards.text:
ah — an autonomous coding agent with abagraph as its brain

ah runs a coding task end to end: it plans, edits, verifies, and refuses to
ship work the gate does not accept. Install with npm, point it at a repo, and
run ah watch to let it work unattended.

golden.query: exponential backoff retry hook
golden.why: The only card whose title carries all three terms; it is the commit that introduced the hook.

golden.query: retyr hook
golden.why: Asking about 'the retry hook' means the commit that introduced retryHook. Requires 'retyr' to survive as a typo of retry rather than dragging the query to the http-client retry-limit chore.

golden.query: verificaton gate blockd the run
golden.why: Two typos over the load-bearing terms; the journal whose gate stage reads 'verdict block' is the run that was blocked.

golden.query: compation drops tool results
golden.why: 'compation' must correct to compaction; the session about dropped tool results is the only card on that failure mode.

golden.query: journalOutcome
golden.why: The identifier is defined by that commit. Many journal cards contain 'journal' and 'outcome' separately, so the whole-token form has to win.

golden.query: parseFrontmatter typed return
golden.why: Only card that names parseFrontmatter; tests that a camelCase query still hits a camelCase title.

golden.query: retryHook double fire
golden.why: The double-fire bug is the fix commit, not the feature commit, even though the identifier appears in the feature commit's title.

golden.query: flaky ordering under load
golden.why: With the path named, the overlapping-tick fix in that exact file beats the debounce fix in watcher.ts and the prime-agent watch loop.

golden.query: rotation and file size
golden.why: Path scoping should pull the store cards up; the rotation commit is the only one about file size.

golden.query: how do we handle errors in tool adapters here
golden.why: A 'how do we do X here' question wants the written rule, not the session that followed it.

golden.query: what is our convention for commit message prefixes
golden.why: CONTRIBUTING.md states the conventional-prefix rule; every commit card is an instance of it, which is exactly the trap.

golden.query: how should a new module start and where do tests go
golden.why: House rules file states both rules verbatim.

golden.query: when is a gate allowed to block
golden.why: The skill states the rule ('a block verdict needs a named regression'); the gate commit is the implementation, the skill is the convention.

golden.query: has migrating the memory weave to abagraph v2 failed before
golden.why: The journal carries the verbatim evidence (tenant header missing on every write). Must beat the default outcome penalty on failed cards.

golden.query: did we already try moving the session store to sqlite
golden.why: The reverted commit is the attempt itself, and the revert marks it failed. A ranker that buries failures loses the one card that answers the question.

golden.query: has the nightly ever failed on a typecheck error
golden.why: Only card whose verify stage records tsc errors.

golden.query: why are session transcripts append-only ndjson
